title: bug: agent Git guard fails closed when moe-agent.ps1 runs under PowerShell 7, because its powershell.exe Set-Acl child inherits pwsh's PSModulePath and cannot load Get-Acl
description: Repro: native Windows (pwsh 7, Git 2.54, node 24.16). In a git-archive snapshot of 04a3e180, `npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts` fails 'lands once, crashes before the receipt…': the pwsh wrapper stops with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED. It fails the same way on HEAD's own bytes. Surfacing the swallowed error shows the guard program's ACL step (moe-agent.ps1, `cp.spawnSync('powershell.exe', … Get-Acl/Set-Acl)`) exiting 1 with "The 'Get-Acl' command was found in the module 'Microsoft.PowerShell.Security', but the module could not be loaded". That is the known PS7→PS5.1 PSModulePath inheritance. Candidate fix: drop PSModulePath from that child's env. Check the sh twin and the other powershell.exe spawns too. Found by task-f33bf7af's Windows gate.

(b) After `const win = ...`, add `const pwsh = win && spawnSync('pwsh.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-Command', 'exit 0'], { timeout: 60000 }).status === 0;`.

(f) In the `if (process.argv[2] !== 'cli') {` block, add the test 'both wrappers embed one guard program, and it keeps PSModulePath from its powershell.exe child'.
- Cut moe-agent.sh between `<<'MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS'\n` and `\nMOE_GIT_GUARD_JS\n`.
- Cut moe-agent.ps1 between `$program = @'\n` and `\n'@\n`.

- Assert that the program matches /'PSMODULEPATH'/. That is the quoted code literal, so the comment alone cannot satisfy it.
- This is the only check of the sh twin: Linux never takes the win32 branch, and parity-check.sh does not compare the programs.

implementationPlan.description:
GREEN, scripts/moe-agent.ps1: function Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard, the `$program = @'...'@` here-string, inside the `if (win) {` block. Any editor works (Edit, apply_patch), as long as the file keeps its UTF-8 BOM (first bytes ef bb bf) and LF-only endings; parity-check.sh enforces the BOM. Never rewrite it through a shell pipeline.
Replace the one line
`        value(cp.spawnSync('powershell.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-EncodedCommand', Buffer.from(acl, 'utf16le').toString('base64')], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 10000, maxBuffer: 1048576 }));`
with these three (8-space indent):
`        // pwsh 7 lists its own modules first in PSModulePath, and a Windows PowerShell 5.1 child that inherits it cannot load Get-Acl.`
`        const psenv = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k]) => k.toUpperCase() !== 'PSMODULEPATH'));`
`        value(cp.spawnSync('powershell.exe', ['-NoProfile', '-NonInteractive', '-EncodedCommand', Buffer.from(acl, 'utf16le').toString('base64')], { env: psenv, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 10000, maxBuffer: 1048576 }));`
Why this shape (each point is measured or sourced in the handoff memory):
- Without the variable, 5.1 builds its own default module path. pwsh repairs PSModulePath only for a powershell.exe it starts directly, never for a grandchild started through node.
- libuv's Windows env injection does not list PSModulePath, so the drop holds (mem:gotcha-windows-libuv-spawn-env-injection).
- Compare keys case-insensitively, because a spread process.env is no longer case-insensitive (the lowercase-count lesson).
- Start from process.env, not the program's `env` const, so the child keeps exactly its old environment minus that one variable.
Error handling is unchanged. A non-zero exit, timeout or spawn error of the ACL child still throws in value(); the catch removes the root, and the wrapper stops with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED (fail closed).
Leave untouched:
- the `& node -` line;
- Invoke-MoeGuardedCommand and Remove-MoeAgentGitGuard, whose span the launcher harnesses cut;
- every launch line, which codexDescriptor.ts pins;
- the rest of the program.
Check: the step-1 PS7 row passes on native Windows from a fresh /mnt/d snapshot with this file overlaid. The twin test stays red until step 3.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: On Windows, the agent Git guard's ACL step runs without an inherited PSModulePath. That step is the powershell.exe Get-Acl/Set-Acl child spawned by the embedded node program in moe-agent.ps1 (Initialize-MoeAgentGitGuard) and in moe-agent.sh (prepare_agent_git_guard). A wrapper started under PowerShell 7, or anywhere below a pwsh ancestor (for example a pwsh CI step running node, which runs the 5.1 wrapper), therefore sets up the guard and launches its CLI instead of failing closed with MOE_AGENT_GIT_GUARD_FAILED.
